summary: Evidence strength: moderate and mostly adjacent. Requirements quality, clarification and requirements-test alignment studies support explicit intent and executable acceptance, but no direct controlled study located compares a complete agentic spec-driven lifecycle with an otherwise matched prompt-driven production workflow.

items.text: Mu et al., ClarifyGPT: Empowering LLM-based Code Generation with Intention Clarification (PACM Software Engineering/FSE 2024), reported that clarification raised GPT-4 Pass@1 from 70.96% to 80.80% on its sanitized MBPP setting and included a small human evaluation. This directly supports refining intent before generation, but not a full versioned specification lifecycle.

Montgomery, Fucci, Bouraffa, Scholz and Maalej, Empirical Research on Requirements Quality: A Systematic Mapping Study (Requirements Engineering, 2022), found a heterogeneous evidence base and only a subset of quality factors repeatedly connected to downstream outcomes. It supports explicit quality criteria while warning that specification volume alone is not evidence of quality.

Wang, Zhao, Wang and Sun, The Role of Requirements Engineering Practices in Agile Development: An Empirical Study (APRES 2014), surveyed 108 practitioners across agile groups and organizations and found requirements practices remained an important prerequisite in agile development. The self-reported, small organizational sample is adjacent evidence, not a causal comparison of agent methods.

Bjarnason, Sharp and Regnell, Improving Requirements-Test Alignment by Prescribing Practices that Mitigate Communication Gaps (Empirical Software Engineering, 2019), grounded Gap Finder in evidence from five companies and evaluated it in an ongoing project; seven of nine prescribed practices were judged relevant. It supports linking requirements and tests, while the formative case study does not establish a universal process.
